question:
A pure (impurity-free) crystalline material $M$ has the following energy information (energy scale in eV):

- Top of valence band: $E_V=-5.0\,\text{eV}$
- Bottom of conduction band: $E_C=-3.9\,\text{eV}$
- Fermi level at $300\,\text{K}$: $E_F=-4.45\,\text{eV}$

(a) Calculate the band gap $E_g$ and classify $M$ as conductor / semiconductor / insulator using band theory.

(b) Using the position of $E_F$ relative to the band edges, decide whether $M$ is behaving as an intrinsic semiconductor at $300\,\text{K}$.

(c) Predict how the conductivity of $M$ changes as temperature is lowered from $300\,\text{K}$ to $0\,\text{K}$, and justify using carrier generation in band theory.

(d) Draw a qualitative energy band diagram showing $E_V$, $E_C$, $E_F$, and the gap clearly.

options.A: $E_g=1.1\,\text{eV}$; $M$ is an intrinsic semiconductor at $300\,\text{K}$; conductivity decreases strongly as $T\to 0\,\text{K}$; band diagram shows $E_F$ at mid-gap.
options.B: $E_g\approx 0$ due to overlap; $M$ is a conductor; conductivity increases as $T\to 0\,\text{K}$; band diagram shows overlapping bands.
options.C: $E_g\approx 5\,\text{eV}$; $M$ is an insulator; conductivity is nearly temperature-independent; band diagram shows a very large gap.
options.D: $E_g=1.1\,\text{eV}$; $M$ is a $p$-type semiconductor; conductivity increases as $T\to 0\,\text{K}$; band diagram shows $E_F$ close to $E_V$.
